explanation: Call int.bit_count() to count the set bits of the nonnegative input integer. The contract limits the representation to 32 bits.
timeComplexity: O(1) for the contract’s at-most-32-bit input; the integer has a bounded number of machine limbs for the built-in population count.
spaceComplexity: O(1) auxiliary space for the bounded-width integer and returned count.
attribution: Original repository-authored Blind75 Python algorithm, promoted from the validated correct fixtures. Collection membership follows Crackr; no external solution service is used.
correctness: bit_count returns the number of ones in an integer’s binary magnitude. Because the input is nonnegative and at most 2^32-1, that magnitude is exactly the required unsigned 32-bit pattern; leading zeros add no ones.
walkthrough: For n=21, the binary magnitude is 10101. bit_count counts its three 1 digits and returns 3.
edgeCases: Inputs are nonnegative; Python’s treatment of negative magnitudes is outside this contract.
